2. The journey, step by step

Each step is pictured as it happened: a screenshot of the Inkcast page the person saw, or a panel rendering the MCP tool call or REST request the client made and the reply it got. 1. Add Inkcast to an MCP client

Step 1 — REST — GET /.well-known/oauth-protected-resource/mcp (rest, 2026-11-05T09:02:09Z)

The client asks the MCP endpoint who protects it: Inkcast's own authorization server.

✓ HTTP 200; the resource names its authorization server

Step 2 — REST — GET /.well-known/oauth-authorization-server (rest, 2026-11-05T09:02:10Z)

Discovery: where to register, authorize and get tokens; PKCE S256 is required.

✓ HTTP 200; metadata lists registration, authorization and token endpoints with S256

Step 3 — dynamic client registration (mcp, 2026-11-05T09:02:10Z)

The client registered itself (RFC 7591); no secret, PKCE instead.

✓ registered as “Walkthrough MCP client” (client_id 01c9f2bc-df81-417d-a1e9-0b5109af1d75), redirect http://localhost:41153/callback
